blind_spots.blind_spot: The company won a Direct-to-Phase-II SBIR specifically for TBI diagnostics, but the entire public product description is framed around a 'telehealth setting' with no discussion of whether the eye-tracking computer-vision model holds up outside controlled clinic/home lighting.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Sunlight glare, dust, and uncontrolled field lighting will degrade a computer-vision eye-tracking algorithm calibrated on clinic/telehealth conditions — the same fragility pattern as any AI model that only works under lab conditions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial PTSD product is the company's primary public-facing narrative; the TBI/military application appears to exist only as a separate, unmarketed SBIR line item.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our diagnostic runs on smartphones, from any location — including a telehealth setting. No specialized equipment or upfront capital investment is needed.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Every open role is a civilian medical-device/SaMD compliance or clinical-operations position; there is no field engineer, ISSO, or DoD-compliance hire despite an active military-relevant SBIR.
blind_spots.operator_reality: FDA SaMD clearance and DoD ATO/CMMC compliance are separate regulatory tracks; a team fully staffed for the FDA path with nobody assigned to the DoD path will stall the moment the TBI diagnostic needs to run on a government network or device.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's core business model and funding history (Series A, civilian mental-health VC) point toward the FDA/commercial healthcare pathway as the organizing priority.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: SaMD Quality Engineer/Sr. Engineer; Director of Clinical Operations

blind_spots.blind_spot: Senseye's own language never mentions TBI or the military at all — every description of the product (workflow, use case, mission statement) is written for civilian mental-health clinicians and patients.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A medic administering a rapid TBI screen in the field needs a workflow built for battlefield triage timing, no dedicated exam room, unreliable connectivity, and a non-clinician administrator — none of which resembles the '10-minute ocular test' telehealth session the company describes everywhere it talks about its product.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The TBI SBIR appears to be an extension of the existing PTSD platform rather than a purpose-built military product, so the deployed-use-case thinking hasn't yet been built into how the company talks about itself.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: We aim to help clinicians personalize care with fast, accurate tools for establishing a clear baseline and tracking outcomes over time.

opener_hook: Your 2025 Direct-to-Phase-II SBIR funds a TBI diagnostic, but the ocular-test workflow on your site is written entirely for a telehealth session — does the field version look different?
what_they_do: Smartphone-based computer-vision eye-tracking platform for objective mental-health diagnosis, built for PTSD in civilian clinical/telehealth settings, with a separate SBIR-funded TBI diagnostic application.
